title: Vegetarian Mapo Tofu
subtitle: Sichuan spiced tofu in fermented bean sauce
excerpt: A bold, numbing, deeply savoury Sichuan dish of silken tofu in a sauce built on fermented black bean paste, chilli, and red miso. This vegetarian version replaces the traditional minced pork with a deeper hit of fermented flavour.
sourceNotes: Mapo tofu originates from the Sichuan province of China, where it has been a street food and home cooking staple for over a century. The name translates roughly as 'pockmarked grandmother's tofu', referring to the elderly woman said to have invented it in Chengdu.

content.text: Silken tofu (about 400g) is the traditional choice for this dish; it has a soft, custard-like texture that contrasts beautifully with the intense sauce. If you prefer something that holds its shape better in the wok, use firm tofu instead, which gives a completely different but equally good result. Handle silken tofu very gently and slide it into the sauce in cubes rather than stirring it.

items.prepNote: thinly sliced, whites and greens separated

content.text: Cut your tofu (silken or firm, about 400g) into 3cm cubes and set aside. If using silken tofu, handle very gently.
Heat the sunflower oil in the wok over a medium heat. Add the doubanjiang and cook, stirring, for 2 minutes until the oil turns red and fragrant.
Add the garlic, ginger, and the white parts of the spring onion. Cook for 1 minute.
Add the gochugaru, miso, and soy sauce. Stir for 30 seconds. Pour in the vegetable stock and bring to a simmer.
Gently slide in the tofu cubes. Spoon the sauce over the tofu carefully, without stirring hard. Simmer for 3 minutes.
Pour in the cornflour slurry in a steady stream, gently swirling the wok rather than stirring, until the sauce has thickened and coats the tofu. Drizzle over the sesame oil.
Serve over steamed rice, scattered with the green spring onion tops.

items.symptom: Silken tofu has broken into small pieces.
items.cause: It was stirred too vigorously in the wok.
items.fix: Swirl the wok gently; use a soft spoon to fold, not stir.

items.cause: Cornflour slurry was not shaken before adding, or heat was too low.
items.fix: Mix slurry again and add over medium-high heat while swirling.

items.cause: Doubanjiang and miso are both salty; soy adds more.
items.fix: Taste before adding soy sauce; reduce or skip if already salty.
